_comment: Krea-2 (K2) MASS-LoRA: train many per-concept adapters at once off ONE frozen base. See krea2/train_mass_lora.py. Every nn.Linear carries a BANK of n_slots adapters ([L, rank, in]); each step packs S slots' samples contiguously on dim 0 and a grouped bmm routes them, so slot i's gradient only touches adapter i. Slots ROTATE: only slots_per_step of them train per step, so cost is independent of how many adapters you are training. 'parallelism' works exactly as in train.py; there is no 'mode' (a bank is always LoRA).
_comment_topology: parallelism 'pipeline' = N GPUs, resident weights. Switch to 'pipeline-offload' if the bank pushes a stage over its GPU, or 'offload' for a single GPU. chunks_per_stage overrides the automatic split (balanced by WEIGHT BYTES; the bank makes block chunks heavier, which the balancer already accounts for).
_comment_slots: group_column's distinct values become the slots (one adapter per artist / character / concept). It must be a column holding ONE plain string per row: the value is used verbatim after .strip(), so normalize casing/punctuation upstream, and a null or empty value means 'skip this row' (which is how you drop collabs and non-artist keys). A JSON column like artist_weights will NOT work — materialize a plain column instead. slots_per_step * per_slot_batch is the PER-MICROBATCH batch and does not depend on the slot count; each active slot sees n_microbatches * per_slot_batch samples per step, which is the batch its learning rate should be read against. min_samples_per_slot drops the long tail (counted on raw rows, before the aspect-ratio filter); max_slots keeps only the largest groups and MUST be set unless the vocabulary is already small, since the bank grows linearly in the slot count.
_comment_slots_tuning: mass_caption_v2 is WIDE and SHALLOW: ~22.8k artists but only 4-8 images each (danbooru median 5, e621 8), against artist_samples' ~25. slot_allowlist is the top 256 artists by AGGREGATE fav_count that have at least 4 images -- requiring 4 costs almost nothing in popularity (the fav floor moves 1841 -> 1694 on danbooru). min_samples_per_slot is inert while an allowlist is set; it is left at 4 to document the floor. resolution_step is 192 rather than 128 for the same reason: 4 live buckets instead of 6 keeps each (slot, bucket) pool around 2-3 images, which cuts the in-step duplication from 2.8x to 2.4x (danbooru) / 2.0x (e621). Measured with dataloaders/probe_mass_lora_plan.py.
_comment_plan: steps_per_epoch defaults to one full pass over every slot's samples. slot_step_balance in [0,1] resolves 'every slot gets the same number of steps' against 'each slot's buckets follow its own aspect-ratio mix' — they conflict for a slot whose data is all one aspect ratio, since it can take at most one seat per step. 0 = follow the data, 1 = equalize step counts and let the narrow buckets dominate. steps_per_epoch stays 6000 while max_steps is 16000: the epoch loop re-cycles the SAME plan (there is no resample() call), so a 16k run is 2.67 passes over one 6000-step plan and each slot lands at ~250 updates (16000 * slots_per_step / n_slots). Leaving the plan length alone is deliberate -- it keeps a resume's `offset` arithmetic simple: offset = initial_global_step % steps_per_epoch.
_comment_bank: bank_exclude_patterns is the memory lever: ['.mlp.'] adapts attention only and roughly halves the bank. bank_dtype 'bf16' matches train.py's LoRA path; 'fp32' doubles the master memory for safer long runs. Layers where rank >= min(in, out) are skipped automatically. Rank 8 x 256 slots costs exactly what rank 32 x 64 slots did (27.3M params/slot, ~14 GB masters + ~14 GB RamTorch grad accumulators on GPU, ~56 GB of AdamW state on the host) -- 4x the artists for the same budget, which is the right trade when a slot only has 5 images to fit. The trainer prints the budget before building the pipeline; read it before scaling n_slots up.
_comment_optim: BankAdamW updates only the active slots and warms up on each slot's OWN step count, so a rarely-scheduled slot still gets a full warmup. Gradient clipping is per slot: a global norm would let one spiking adapter shrink everyone else's update. LR SURVEY (2026-08-31, before touching lr): alpha == rank == 8 means the LoRA scale alpha/r is exactly 1.0, and an LR quoted without its alpha is meaningless (QLoRA states alpha is proportional to lr). At scale 1.0 the references converge on 1e-4: diffusers' train_dreambooth_lora_{flux,sd3}.py default, ai-toolkit's Flux/SD3.5/Qwen-Image configs, and HF's official Flux LoRA recipe -- which is scale 1.0, 1e-4, constant LR, 12B rectified-flow DiT at an effective batch of 4, i.e. this run exactly. kohya's Flux doc and OneTrainer quote 1e-4 / 3e-4 but at alpha 1 over rank 16, i.e. scale 0.0625, so in effective terms they are BELOW us. 1e-3 was considered and rejected: at scale 1.0 it is ~10x the Flux recipe, and SimpleTuner names it as the failure case for a 12B model ('LoRA at 1e-3 might totally roast the thing') -- its own 1e-3 ceiling assumes an EMA network and a long warmup, neither of which exist here. rsLoRA's alpha/sqrt(r) argument gives rank 8 only ~1.4x headroom over the rank-16 recipes, not 10x. Practical ceiling is ~2e-4; above ~5e-4 expect burned previews before the loss shows anything. If it still underfits, drop alpha rather than raise lr. warmup 20 looks short against the 100-500 the public trainers use, but those count GLOBAL steps: here it is per SLOT, a slot only ever sees ~250 updates in a 16k run, and betas (0.9, 0.95) put the second-moment timescale at 1/(1-b2) = 20 steps, so 20 is proportionate.
_comment_eval: Previews render ONE slot per eval, round-robin over that step's active set, named after the group value. save_every_n_steps writes the WHOLE bank, so keep it conservative — at rank 16 that is ~59M params per slot.
_comment_ckpt: Path to the K2 DiT base weights (safetensors). See checkpoints/README.md. bank_checkpoint resumes a mass run; its sibling slots.json restores the per-slot step counts.

parquet_dataloader._comment_captions: One caption column is drawn per row at load time, weights normalised over the columns that row actually has (all five are 100% populated here). tags and midjourney_style_summary carry 2x the weight of the prose bands, so the adapter sees the two prompt styles it will mostly be driven with twice as often. Only 'tags' is tag_based: is_tag_based drives comma-shuffling, and while the midjourney band is also comma-separated its order is meaningful (medium and artist first), so shuffling it would destroy the convention it exists to teach. brief_summary and 10_word_summary never name the artist, which is deliberate -- the adapter carries the style, so those two teach it to fire without a trigger phrase.

_comment_resume: RESUMED from step 2700 after the caption fix (per-VISIT band resampling) and the lr bump to 2e-4. Three keys move together on a resume: bank_checkpoint supplies the masters, initial_global_step continues the step accounting against the absolute max_steps, and slots.json NEXT TO the checkpoint restores the per-slot step counts (so warmup and Adam bias correction stay honest per adapter). offset is deliberately 0 this time, NOT from step 2700: the caption fix removed a per-row rng.choices() call from the pool build, which shifts the shared RNG stream that _assign_bucket and _plan_steps consume, so the plan for this seed is no longer the plan the old run was walking. An offset would skip a fair PREFIX of a DIFFERENT schedule rather than resuming the old one, which buys nothing -- the deficit planner is fair within each pass and slots.json already carries the history. What is still NOT restored is the AdamW moments; with betas (0.9, 0.95) they respool in ~20 slot-steps, and warmup 20 covers exactly that. Set bank_checkpoint null and initial_global_step 0 to start clean.
_comment_captions: All five bands a row has are kept, and ONE IS DRAWN PER VISIT (not per row at load time) -- a slot holds ~5 images and revisits each ~250 times, so a load-time draw pinned every image to a single band for the whole run and an adapter could never see `tags` on more than one or two of its images. Weights are renormalised over the bands a row actually has. tags and midjourney_style_summary carry 2x the prose bands, so the adapter sees the two prompt styles it will mostly be driven with twice as often. Only `tags` is tag_based: is_tag_based drives comma-shuffling, and while the midjourney band is also comma-separated its order is meaningful (medium and artist first), so shuffling it would destroy the convention it exists to teach. brief_summary and 10_word_summary never name the artist, which is deliberate -- the adapter carries the style, so those two teach it to fire without a trigger phrase. Guarded by dataloaders/check_mass_lora_captions.py.
